verdict: Sales jumped 25% as datacenter demand powered Electrical Solutions, but the interest bill on acquisition debt held net profit growth to 3%.

segments.name: Utility Solutions
segments.note: Grid infrastructure and automation gear sold to electric utilities — connectors, enclosures and controls for the power grid.

segments.name: Electrical Solutions
segments.note: Wiring devices, lighting controls and datacenter electrical gear; organic sales rose 22% and acquisitions (led by NSI) added 29 points.

opex.name: Selling & administrative
opex.note: Selling and administrative costs — sales teams, marketing and the back office.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $58M — up from $14M a year ago on debt taken on for the NSI and DMC Power acquisitions — plus $5M of other expense.

takeaways.title: Half the growth was bought
takeaways.text: Organic sales rose 11% — strong on its own — while acquisitions, led by NSI in Electrical Solutions, contributed about 13 points of the 25% growth.

takeaways.title: Electrical Solutions is the engine
takeaways.text: Electrical Solutions sales leapt 51% to $845M on datacenter demand and the NSI deal; Utility Solutions grew a steadier 9% to $1,028M.

takeaways.title: Debt ate the profit growth
takeaways.text: Operating profit rose 24%, but net interest expense quadrupled to $58M after acquisition borrowing, so net income rose just 3% to $265M.

oneTimers: Adjusted results exclude $62M of amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets and $6M of transaction, integration and separation costs — that is why adjusted EPS ($5.91) sits well above GAAP EPS ($4.94), and adjusted operating profit was $477M vs $409M GAAP.
